definition: Of, resembling, or as white as snow; having the pure, cold whiteness characteristic of fresh-fallen snow.
etymology: From Latin niveus, meaning snowy or snow-white, itself from nix, nivis, meaning snow. The same root gives English neve, the compacted granular snow of a glacier's upper reaches, and the rare verb nive, once used by poets to mean to snow. Latin nix is cousin to Greek nipha and traces back to the Proto-Indo-European root sneigwh, to snow, ancestor also of the Germanic word that became English snow itself — so the whole family has been describing the same cold whiteness since before writing existed.
usage: By the first week of November the hills north of town had gone niveous overnight, that sudden shocking white that makes the previous day feel like a different season entirely.
